questions.stem: A broker's neighbor is selling a cabin to a friend with no broker involved. The neighbor asks the broker to fill in the deed and offers $150 for the paperwork. What should the broker do?
choices: Accept, as long as the broker uses a Commission-approved form
Accept without the fee, so the work falls under the Conway-Bogue conditions
Decline, because the broker isn't brokering this transaction
Accept if both parties sign a written consent to the broker's help
questions.explanation: Brokers may complete standard forms only in transactions where they are acting as the broker, and never for a separate fee. Preparing a deed for someone else's private sale is the unauthorized practice of law, even without a fee or with the parties' consent.

questions.stem: A commercial buyer wants to send a letter of intent before negotiating a full contract. If the broker completes the letter of intent as a standard form, what must it say on its face?
choices: That it becomes binding once both parties sign it
That it replaces any Commission-approved contract for the deal
That the broker drafted it with help from the firm's attorney
That it is nonbinding
questions.explanation: A letter of intent is one of the standard forms a broker may complete, but it must state on its face that it is nonbinding. The binding agreement still goes on the appropriate contract form.

questions.stem: A buyer's broker is helping a client buy a new home, and the builder insists on using its own purchase contract. What must the broker do?
choices: Rewrite the builder's contract to match the Commission-approved residential contract
Advise the buyer in writing to get legal advice from an attorney before signing
Refuse to proceed, because only Commission-approved contracts may be used
Attach the Commission-approved contract as an addendum that overrides the builder's form
questions.explanation: A broker may work with a principal-supplied contract, such as a builder's, by inserting transaction-specific information, but Commission rules require advising the client in writing to consult an attorney before signing. The broker doesn't rewrite or override the principal's form.

questions.stem: A section of a Commission-approved contract doesn't apply to the transaction. How should the broker handle it?
choices: Keep the section caption and mark the text as omitted or not applicable
Delete the whole section, including its caption, so the printed form is shorter
Erase the section and retype the remaining paragraphs in order
Leave it unchanged and tell the parties orally to ignore it
questions.explanation: When a section doesn't apply, its caption stays and the text is marked as omitted or not applicable. Printed text is never erased, and the broker must explain every change to the principal.

questions.stem: A listing broker who is not a party to the sale wants to add a sentence to Additional Provisions stating that neither brokerage is liable for the condition of the roof. May the broker do this?
choices: Yes, because Additional Provisions are not Commission-approved language anyway
Yes, if the seller initials the sentence
Yes, as long as the buyer's broker agrees to it in writing
No; a broker who isn't a party may not add a clause protecting the broker
questions.explanation: Commission rules bar a broker who isn't a party from adding an exculpatory clause that protects the broker. Additional Provisions are for recording what the parties agreed to, not for shielding the broker.

questions.stem: A landlord client asks his broker to use the Commission-approved residential lease. What is accurate?
choices: The broker must use the Income-Residential contract's lease addendum
The Commission has no approved leases or property management agreements
The broker may draft a lease because leasing isn't the practice of law
The Commission's lease is required whenever the broker manages the property
questions.explanation: There are no Commission-approved leases or property management agreements. The lease has to come from another permitted source, such as an attorney-drafted form or one the owner supplies; the broker never drafts it.

questions.stem: A new version of a Commission-approved form became mandatory on January 1. On January 10, a broker's transaction software still fills in the old version. What is the issue?
choices: None, because the old version stays valid until the date printed on it
None, as long as both parties initial each page of the old version
It violates the requirement to use the Commission-approved form
The broker must get the Commission's permission before using the old version
questions.explanation: Each revision has a mandatory-use date. Using an outdated version after its replacement becomes mandatory violates the requirement to use the Commission-approved form, so brokers must make sure their software has the current version.

questions.stem: A buyer's broker fills in the property section of the residential contract with only the street address. What is missing?
choices: Nothing, because a street address fully identifies the property
The county assessor's parcel number, which replaces the address
A new survey, which must be attached to identify the property
The legal description, which an address alone can't replace
questions.explanation: The contract identifies the property by its legal description. A street address alone isn't enough to identify real property for a sale.

questions.stem: The home has leased solar panels. Under the residential contract, what is needed for the panel lease to carry over to the buyer?
choices: Buyer's choice to assume it, plus the lessor's written approval
Nothing, because attached items are automatically included in the sale
A bill of sale from the seller listing the panels as personal property
The listing broker's written confirmation that the lease is transferable
questions.explanation: Leased items and encumbered inclusions require the buyer to choose whether to assume the obligation, plus written approval from the lessor or lienholder before closing. Leased panels belong to the lessor, so a bill of sale from the seller can't convey them.

questions.stem: A home sale includes deeded water rights and shares of water stock. How does the residential contract handle them?
choices: They pass automatically with the deed, so the contract doesn't mention them
They have their own subsection and a Water Rights Examination Deadline
They must be sold under a separate Land contract
They are listed as exclusions and conveyed after closing
questions.explanation: Water rights, including deeded rights, well rights and water stock, have their own subsection in the residential contract and a Water Rights Examination Deadline for the buyer's review.

questions.stem: In the residential contract's purchase price section, what is a seller concession?
choices: A cut in the purchase price that the seller agrees to after a low appraisal
Earnest money the seller agrees to refund if the loan is denied
A credit to the buyer at closing that can cover costs the lender allows
A payment from the seller to the buyer's brokerage firm
questions.explanation: A seller concession is a credit from the seller to the buyer at closing that can cover costs the buyer's lender allows. It isn't a price reduction or compensation to a brokerage.

questions.stem: Under the residential contract, when does the buyer deliver the earnest money if no Alternative Earnest Money Deadline is set?
choices: Within 3 days after the New Loan Application Deadline
At closing, to the closing company
After the Inspection Resolution Deadline passes
With the contract
questions.explanation: The buyer delivers earnest money with the contract unless the parties set an Alternative Earnest Money Deadline. The Earnest Money Holder keeps it in trust for both parties and may transfer it to the closing company at or before closing.

questions.stem: The parties write "N/A" next to the Appraisal Deadline in the Dates and Deadlines table. What is the effect?
choices: That deadline and the provision tied to it don't apply
The deadline defaults to MEC plus 10 days
The deadline becomes the same as the Closing Date
The contract isn't binding until the parties fill in a date
questions.explanation: A deadline left blank or marked N/A or Deleted means that deadline and the provision tied to it don't apply. It doesn't default to another date or keep the contract from forming.

questions.stem: A buyer's offer has an Acceptance Deadline of 8:00 p.m. Friday. The seller signs at 7:30 p.m. Friday, but neither the buyer nor the buyer's broker learns of the signature until Saturday morning. What is the result?
choices: A contract formed at 7:30 p.m., when the seller signed
The offer expired without timely notice of acceptance
A contract formed, because the seller signed before the deadline
The deadline extends automatically to the next business day
questions.explanation: An offer expires unless both parties sign and the offering party receives notice of acceptance by the Acceptance Deadline. Signing alone isn't enough.

questions.stem: The seller will carry back part of the price. Under the residential contract, who may terminate if the financing documents are unsatisfactory?
choices: Only the buyer, by the New Loan Terms Deadline
Only the seller, by the Disapproval of Buyer's Credit Information Deadline
Either party, by the Seller or Private Financing Deadline
Neither party, because seller financing isn't a contingency
questions.explanation: Under the seller or private financing provision, either party may terminate if the financing documents are unsatisfactory in that party's sole subjective discretion, by the Seller or Private Financing Deadline.

questions.stem: The buyer delivers a timely objection to a low appraisal. The seller won't lower the price, nothing is agreed by the Appraisal Resolution Deadline, and the buyer hasn't withdrawn the objection. What happens?
choices: The buyer must close at the contract price
The seller must lower the price to the appraised value
The buyer gets 10 more days to obtain a second appraisal
The contract terminates
questions.explanation: An unresolved appraisal objection terminates the contract at the Appraisal Resolution Deadline unless the buyer withdraws the objection in writing before then. The seller isn't required to cut the price.

questions.stem: A new Improvement Location Certificate shows the garage sits over the setback line. What may the buyer do under the residential contract?
choices: Terminate or object by the New ILC or New Survey Objection Deadline
Nothing, because survey and ILC matters are handled only by the title insurance policy
Require the seller to move the garage before closing
Delay closing until the county grants a variance
questions.explanation: The buyer may terminate or object over an unsatisfactory ILC or survey by the New ILC or New Survey Objection Deadline. If an objection isn't resolved, the contract terminates unless the buyer withdraws it.

questions.stem: Which home requires the lead-based paint disclosure in a Colorado residential sale?
choices: A home built in 1985 with its original exterior paint
Any home with a basement, regardless of its age
A home whose building permit was issued in 1976
A home built in 1990 that was repainted last year
questions.explanation: Lead-based paint disclosure applies to dwellings built, or with a building permit issued, before January 1, 1978. A 1976 permit qualifies.

questions.stem: A seller knows methamphetamine was once manufactured in the home, and the property was never remediated to state standards. What does the residential contract require?
choices: Nothing, because the buyer's inspection will reveal it
The seller must disclose it
The broker must report it to the Real Estate Commission
The seller may disclose it only with the buyer's written consent
questions.explanation: The seller must disclose known methamphetamine manufacture, use or storage unless the property was remediated to state standards. It isn't left to the buyer's inspection.

questions.stem: What does the residential contract say about radon?
choices: The seller must have the home tested for radon before it is listed for sale
The buyer waives radon claims by closing
Radon is covered only in the Commercial contract
It recommends a test; the seller gives known results
questions.explanation: The contract includes a state health department advisory strongly recommending a radon test before buying, and the seller must provide any radon test results the seller knows of. It doesn't require the seller to test.

questions.stem: A home has a gas furnace and bedrooms. Under Colorado law, where must an operational carbon monoxide alarm be installed?
choices: Within 15 feet of each bedroom entrance
Within 5 feet of the furnace or other fuel-fired appliance
Inside the attached garage, near the door to the house
In the main hallway, at least 30 feet from any bedroom
questions.explanation: When a home has a fuel-fired heater or appliance, a fireplace or an attached garage, plus a bedroom, Colorado law requires an operational carbon monoxide alarm within 15 feet of each bedroom entrance (or where the building code requires).

questions.stem: Under the residential contract's source of water provision, what does the buyer acknowledge when the home is served by a well?
choices: That the State Engineer has inspected the well
That the seller warrants the well's water quality
Receiving the water source information and well permit information
That the buyer will apply for a new well permit before the closing date
questions.explanation: The buyer acknowledges receiving the source-of-water information and, for a well, the well permit information. The seller doesn't warrant water quality.

questions.stem: The buyer's inspector damages a deck railing during the inspection, and the buyer later terminates the contract. Who is responsible for the damage?
choices: The seller, because the contract terminated
The buyer, whose obligation survives termination
The listing broker, who allowed the inspection
No one, because inspections are at the seller's risk
questions.explanation: The buyer pays for inspections, must repair damage they cause and indemnifies the seller. Those obligations survive termination of the contract.

questions.stem: A contract is conditioned on the sale of the buyer's current home. That home hasn't sold, and the Conditional Sale Deadline passes with no notice from the buyer. What is the result?
choices: The contract terminates automatically and the earnest money is returned
The deadline extends until the buyer's home sells
The seller must accept a new closing date
The buyer has lost the right to terminate under that contingency
questions.explanation: A buyer with a conditional sale contingency must terminate by the Conditional Sale Deadline or lose that right. Time is of the essence, so the deadline doesn't extend on its own.

questions.stem: Closing has occurred, but the seller doesn't deliver possession at the Possession Date and Time. No occupancy agreement was signed. What does the residential contract provide?
choices: The closing is unwound and the deed goes back to the seller
The buyer must wait 30 days before taking any action
Eviction, plus the contract's per-day amount and damages
The buyer's only remedy is to keep the earnest money
questions.explanation: A seller who holds over after the Possession Date and Time is subject to eviction and owes the per-day amount set in the contract plus actual damages. A seller who plans to stay should sign a Post-Closing Occupancy Agreement.

questions.stem: Before closing, a fire damages a home under contract for $500,000. Repairs are estimated at $65,000. What right does the buyer have?
choices: The buyer may terminate, because the damage exceeds 10% of the price
None, because the seller's homeowner's insurance will cover the repair costs
The buyer may demand a $65,000 price reduction
The buyer must close and file an insurance claim
questions.explanation: If casualty damage exceeds 10% of the purchase price, or the property isn't repaired by the Closing Date, the buyer may terminate. $65,000 is 13% of $500,000.

questions.stem: After closing, the actual property tax bill turns out higher than the figure used to prorate taxes. Additional Provisions say nothing about it. What is the result?
choices: The seller must pay the difference when the bill arrives
The closing company re-prorates using the actual bill
The buyer and seller split the difference equally
The proration stands, because prorations are final
questions.explanation: Under the residential contract, prorations are final unless the Additional Provisions say otherwise, so neither party owes an adjustment after closing.

questions.stem: The buyer terminates by a timely Notice to Terminate under the inspection provision. The buyer isn't in default. What happens to the earnest money?
choices: The seller keeps it as liquidated damages
It is returned to the buyer
It is split equally between buyer and seller
It goes to the listing brokerage as compensation
questions.explanation: When the contract terminates, the earnest money goes back to the buyer unless the buyer is in default. A proper, timely termination isn't a default.

questions.stem: In a Counterproposal, the seller changes the price and leaves the Closing Date line blank. What happens to the Closing Date?
choices: It is deleted and must be renegotiated
It defaults to 30 days after acceptance
It stays as in the proposed contract
The seller may choose it later
questions.explanation: In the Counterproposal tables, a blank or "No Change" leaves the term as it was in the proposed contract, and "Deleted" removes the provision. All other terms stay the same.

questions.stem: A buyer uses the Extension or Termination of Contract form to ask for more time. The seller doesn't sign Part I, and the time for acceptance passes. What is the effect of Part II?
choices: It acts as the buyer's notice to terminate
The extension takes effect anyway because the seller didn't object
The contract continues under its original deadlines
The seller must sign an Agreement to Revive
questions.explanation: If both parties don't sign Part I and the requesting party doesn't receive notice of acceptance in time, Part II works as the requesting party's notice to terminate, based on the contract provisions checked.

questions.stem: Buyer and seller sign an Inspection Resolution in which the seller agrees to give the buyer a repair credit. Who else should the buyer give a copy to?
choices: The county assessor
The Real Estate Commission
The owners' association board
The buyer's lender
questions.explanation: An Inspection Resolution amends the contract, and repairs or credits can change the loan, so the buyer should give the lender a copy.

questions.stem: The contract has no Time of Day Deadline. On the Inspection Termination Deadline, the buyer emails a Notice to Terminate that reaches the seller's broker's inbox at 11:52 p.m. Mountain Time. The seller reads it the next morning. Is the termination timely?
choices: No, because the seller personally didn't receive it until the next day
Yes, because receipt by the seller's broker before 11:59 p.m. counts
No, because termination notices can't be delivered by email
Yes, but only if the seller signs it
questions.explanation: Before closing, delivery to the party's broker or brokerage counts as delivery to the party, and a day ends at 11:59 p.m. Mountain Time when no Time of Day Deadline applies. With a 5:00 p.m. Time of Day Deadline, the same email would be late.

questions.stem: A seller tells the listing broker not to present offers below $600,000. How must this limit be handled?
choices: The broker may follow it based on the seller's oral instruction
The broker must refuse, since every offer must always be presented
Explain pros and cons, then put the limit in the listing contract
The broker must get each buyer's broker's consent to the limit
questions.explanation: A listing broker may limit which offers are presented only after explaining the pros and cons to the seller, and the limit must be written into the listing contract. An oral instruction isn't enough.

questions.stem: A seller receives four offers and wants to send Counterproposals to all four buyers at once. What is the main risk?
choices: More than one buyer could accept, binding the seller twice
Counterproposals can be sent only to the highest offer
The listing broker loses the right to compensation
The original offers stay open and the seller can still accept any of them
questions.explanation: Each Counterproposal is an offer the buyer can accept. Countering several buyers at once can create more than one binding contract if more than one accepts, so this strategy needs care and usually a lawyer.

questions.stem: Under the Exclusive Right-to-Sell Listing Contract, what must happen before the listing broker accepts compensation from someone other than the seller?
choices: The buyer must consent orally
The Commission must approve it
Nothing, if the amount is less than the listing fee
The seller must consent in writing
questions.explanation: The listing contract bars the broker from accepting third-party compensation without the seller's written consent.

questions.stem: During the holdover period, the seller signs an exclusive listing with a new firm, which earns a commission selling to a Submitted Prospect of the first firm. Neither Will/Will Not box was checked in the first listing. Does the seller owe the first firm?
choices: Yes, because the buyer was a Submitted Prospect
No; with neither box checked, nothing is owed to the first firm
Yes, and each firm receives half the commission
No, because holdover clauses can't be enforced in Colorado residential listings
questions.explanation: The Will/Will Not box decides whether the seller still owes the first firm when another firm earns a commission under a new exclusive listing signed during holdover. If neither box is checked, the seller doesn't owe the first firm.

questions.stem: Under an Exclusive Right-to-Buy Contract, the buyer's broker's fee is more than the listing firm pays. When does the buyer owe the unpaid balance?
choices: Only if it was disclosed in writing before the purchase contract
Always, since the buyer owes the full fee no matter who else pays any part of it
Never, because only sellers pay brokerage compensation
Only if the seller refuses to pay it at closing
questions.explanation: Amounts paid by the seller or the listing firm count toward the buyer's broker's compensation. The buyer owes any unpaid balance only if the broker disclosed that amount in writing before the buyer signed a contract with the seller.

questions.stem: A buyer under an Exclusive Right-to-Buy Contract wants to know whether registered sex offenders live near a home. What does the contract tell the buyer?
choices: The seller must disclose any nearby offenders on the Seller's Property Disclosure
The buyer's broker must research it and report in writing
The buyer should get that information from local law enforcement
It is listed in the title commitment
questions.explanation: The Exclusive Right-to-Buy Contract's Megan's Law paragraph tells the buyer that if the presence of a registered sex offender matters, the buyer must get that information from local law enforcement.

questions.stem: A contract includes the Short Sale Addendum. The lienholder's written acceptance hasn't arrived by the Short Sale Acceptance Deadline. What happens?
choices: The seller must pay the shortfall at closing
The contract terminates
The buyer must wait until the lienholder decides
The deadline extends automatically by 30 days
questions.explanation: Under the Short Sale Addendum, if the lienholder's written acceptance isn't received by the Short Sale Acceptance Deadline, the contract terminates. Changing that deadline would take an Agreement to Amend/Extend.

questions.stem: A short sale closes after the lienholder accepts less than the loan balance. What does the Short Sale Addendum warn the seller about?
choices: The lender's acceptance automatically forgives any balance remaining on the loan
The buyer becomes responsible for the deficiency
The listing broker must pay any deficiency from the commission
Unless released in writing, the seller may still owe the deficiency
questions.explanation: The seller may still owe the deficiency unless the lender releases it in writing, and forgiven debt can be taxable. The form strongly urges legal and tax advice.

questions.stem: Under the Commission-approved Closing Instructions, which deed won't the closing company prepare, so that the buyer or seller must supply it or give written instructions for it?
choices: A personal representative's deed
A statutory special warranty deed
A statutory bargain and sale deed
A statutory quitclaim deed
questions.explanation: The closing company prepares standard deeds the contract calls for: general warranty, special warranty, bargain and sale and quitclaim deeds. For a personal representative's or trustee's deed, or a warranty deed listing exceptions beyond the statutory ones, the buyer or seller must provide the deed or written instructions for preparing it.

questions.stem: A seller carrying back financing uses the Commission's Deed of Trust (Due on Transfer – Creditworthy). What does that version allow?
choices: The borrower may transfer the property freely, with no acceleration
The lender may accelerate on any transfer, regardless of the new owner
Acceleration if the new owner after a transfer isn't creditworthy
The Public Trustee must approve each transfer of the property
questions.explanation: The Due on Transfer – Creditworthy deed of trust lets the lender accelerate if the property is transferred to someone who isn't creditworthy. The Strict version allows acceleration on any transfer, and the Assumable version isn't due on transfer.

questions.stem: A buyer is purchasing a small retail building and wants time for a Phase I environmental review and an ADA evaluation. Which Commission contract is built for this?
choices: Contract to Buy and Sell Real Estate (Residential)
Contract to Buy and Sell Real Estate (Commercial)
Contract to Buy and Sell Real Estate (Land)
Contract to Buy and Sell Real Estate (Income-Residential)
questions.explanation: Office, retail, industrial and mixed-use property uses the Commercial contract, which has deadlines for environmental (Phase I/II) review and an ADA evaluation.

questions.stem: A broker is listing a working ranch with grazing land, water rights and two houses. Which approach fits the current Commission forms?
choices: The Commission-approved Farm and Ranch contract
The Residential contract, because people live in the houses on the ranch
The Commercial contract with no addendum
The Land contract with a Residential Addendum for the houses
questions.explanation: There is no farm and ranch contract on the current list. A ranch typically uses the Land contract, which covers water, minerals and growing crops, with a Residential Addendum to bring in the residential disclosures for the houses.

questions.stem: Under the Manufactured Home Contract to Buy and Sell (Lot Lease Only), the park owner refuses to approve the buyer as a tenant. What may the buyer do?
choices: Terminate, since park approval is a condition of the deal
Close anyway and negotiate a lease with the park later
Require the seller to move the home to another park at the seller's cost
Assign the contract to the park owner
questions.explanation: The Lot Lease Only contract depends on the park owner approving the buyer and the home in writing and either assigning the lease or signing a new one. The buyer may terminate if the lease or the approval terms are unsatisfactory.

questions.stem: A seller owns 10 acres and the manufactured home on it, which still has a certificate of title. The land and home are being sold together. Which Commission forms fit?
choices: Manufactured Home Contract to Buy and Sell (Lot Lease Only)
Residential contract alone, since the home is a dwelling
Land contract with the Manufactured Home Addendum
Land contract alone, since the home is personal property
questions.explanation: When the land is sold along with the manufactured home, the Land (or Commercial) contract is used with the Manufactured Home Addendum, which adds the serial number, VIN, certificate-of-title steps and a UCC search. The Residential contract has no manufactured home provisions, and the Lot Lease Only contract is for homes on rented spaces.

questions.stem: A broker's firm signs a guaranteed buy-out with a listing client using the Licensee Buy-Out Addendum. How must the firm treat the listing?
choices: Mark it as under contract in the MLS
Withdraw it from the MLS and other advertising until the buy-out closes
Mark it as sold to the firm
Keep marketing it as active in the MLS and other advertising
questions.explanation: The Commission's position on guaranteed buy-outs requires the broker to keep marketing the property as active. The seller may terminate the buy-out at any time, and the listing stays in effect.

questions.stem: Under the Post-Closing Occupancy Agreement, how is the seller's security deposit handled?
choices: The listing brokerage holds it and returns it at the next closing
The buyer holds it, up to two months' rent
The closing company holds it and releases it 60 days after closing
No deposit is allowed under the form
questions.explanation: The buyer holds the security deposit, which can't exceed two months' rent, and returns it within 30 days after the term ends, as Colorado law requires. Rent is paid to the buyer in advance at closing.

questions.stem: A broker selling her own rental property outside her firm has her attorney prepare the contract instead of using a Commission form. What must that form state?
choices: That the Commission reviewed it
That the buyer has waived the right to consult a separate attorney
Conspicuously, that it is not a Commission-approved form
That the broker acts as the buyer's transaction-broker
questions.explanation: A broker who is a party may have their own attorney prepare a form, but it must conspicuously state that it is not a Commission-approved form. The broker must also disclose their licensed status in writing.

questions.stem: Which property is most likely part of a common interest community under CCIOA?
choices: A townhome whose owner must pay assessments for shared grounds
A rural parcel with its own private well, septic system and no shared property
A single-family home in a city with no HOA
A rental house owned by an LLC
questions.explanation: A common interest community is real estate where owning a unit or lot obligates the owner to pay for common property or other units' expenses. Condominiums, most townhome communities and planned subdivisions with an HOA are typical.

questions.stem: An HOA's declaration bans all political signs and drought-tolerant landscaping. An owner says CCIOA limits such bans. Which statement is accurate?
choices: The declaration controls, because owners agreed to it at purchase
Owners can waive CCIOA's protections in the declaration
CCIOA limits such bans, and owners generally can't waive it
Only the Real Estate Commission can decide the issue
questions.explanation: CCIOA limits what associations can prohibit, including flags, political signs, drought-tolerant landscaping and EV chargers. Its protections can't be waived or varied by agreement except where the Act allows.

questions.stem: An HOA charges each owner a one-time $4,000 to replace the clubhouse roof. This charge is a
choices: regular assessment
working-capital contribution
status letter fee
special assessment
questions.explanation: A special assessment is a one-time charge for a specific need, such as a new roof. Regular assessments are the recurring dues that fund the budget, including reserves.

questions.stem: How is an HOA's statutory lien for assessments perfected under CCIOA?
choices: By recording a separate lien notice each time an owner falls behind
By recording the declaration
By filing a claim with the HOA Information and Resource Center
By obtaining a court judgment against the owner
questions.explanation: Recording the declaration perfects the association's lien, so no separate lien filing is needed. The lien is extinguished unless the association starts enforcement within six years after the full amount of assessments becomes due.

questions.stem: A unit owner delivers a written request to the HOA's registered agent by certified mail for a statement of unpaid assessments. The HOA never responds. What is the effect?
choices: The HOA can't assert a lien for assessments due as of the request date
The HOA may assert whatever amount it later finds was owed on that date
The request expires and must be resent
The buyer becomes liable for any unpaid assessments
questions.explanation: The association must furnish the statement within 14 calendar days of a proper written request, and the statement binds it. If it isn't furnished, the association can't assert a lien for assessments due as of the request date.

questions.stem: Under the Commission residential contract, who pays an association special assessment for a new community pool that was already completed when the buyer signed the contract?
choices: The buyer, because assessments follow ownership
The buyer and seller equally
The seller
Whoever the HOA board designates
questions.explanation: A checkbox decides who pays special assessments levied before closing, but the seller pays special assessments for improvements already installed as of the buyer's signing date.

questions.stem: A buyer asks the broker whether the HOA's declaration would allow her to run a home daycare. What should the broker do?
choices: Interpret the declaration and tell the buyer whether it's allowed
Have her read the documents and get legal advice
Ask the HOA manager for a binding ruling
Tell the buyer that HOA rules can't restrict home businesses
questions.explanation: Brokers should point out restrictions that matter to the buyer and calendar the association document deadlines, but they shouldn't interpret the documents. The buyer should read them and get legal advice on anything complicated.

questions.stem: A buyer's title objection isn't resolved by the Title Resolution Deadline, and the buyer didn't withdraw it. A week later both parties want to go ahead on the same terms with new deadlines. Which form fits?
choices: Agreement to Amend/Extend Contract
Counterproposal
Title-Related Objection Notice
Agreement to Revive Contract
questions.explanation: An unresolved title objection terminates the contract at the Title Resolution Deadline unless the buyer withdraws it. A terminated contract can't be amended; the Agreement to Revive Contract states the termination date, ratifies the contract and sets new deadlines.

questions.stem: The appraisal comes in low and the buyer timely objects. Before the Appraisal Resolution Deadline, the parties agree to cut the price by $10,000. How should they document it?
choices: An Agreement to Amend/Extend Contract signed before the deadline
A Counterproposal from the seller
A note in the buyer's broker's transaction file
An Agreement to Revive Contract signed once the resolution deadline has passed
questions.explanation: Changes to a signed contract, such as a price reduction after an appraisal objection, are made with an Agreement to Amend/Extend signed by both parties. It has to be done before the Appraisal Resolution Deadline, or the unresolved objection terminates the contract.

questions.stem: A broker lists her own home for sale through her own brokerage firm. Which statement is accurate?
choices: She may use any attorney-drafted contract she prefers
She needn't disclose her license because she is the owner
She uses Commission forms and discloses her license in writing
She must have another firm list the home
questions.explanation: A broker selling her own property through her firm must use the Commission-approved forms when appropriate and, as a principal, must disclose in writing that she's licensed. A broker selling outside the firm may use other forms.
